title: Arshdeep, Gurnoor and Nabi to Stay Back for India's New Zealand Test Preparations
excerpt: India will retain three ODI pacers in New Zealand as net bowlers and reserves for the two-Test series, while five Test squad members skip the last two ODIs to open a Wellington camp on November 11.
body:
• Arshdeep Singh, Gurnoor Brar and Auqib Nabi will stay back in New Zealand after the ODI series to help India prepare for the two Tests, batting coach Sitanshu Kotak confirmed in Hamilton.
  • None of the three is in the Test squad; they will serve as net bowlers and standby reserves, joining the Test contingent on November 16 after the fifth ODI.
  • Test squad members Shubman Gill, KL Rahul, Mohammed Siraj, Anshul Kamboj and Kuldeep Yadav will skip the last two ODIs and open a red-ball camp in Wellington on November 11.
  • The two-match World Test Championship series starts at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on November 19, with the second Test in Christchurch from November 27.

India will keep three of their ODI fast bowlers in New Zealand after the one-day series ends, as the team shifts its focus to the two-match Test series against the Black Caps. Batting coach Sitanshu Kotak confirmed on Monday that Arshdeep Singh, Gurnoor Brar and Auqib Nabi are expected to stay back to support the Test squad's preparations, even though none of the three has been named in the Test squad.

Speaking at a pre-match press conference in Hamilton on the eve of the third ODI, Kotak was tentative on the names but clear on the plan. "I think three bowlers," he said. "Gurnoor, maybe Nabi, and I think Arsh is also staying back." According to ESPNcricinfo, the trio will help the Test squad as net bowlers and reserve players, giving India's batters sustained practice against left-arm and right-arm pace in local conditions before the series opener.

The logic is built on form. The three pacers have been central to India's 2-0 lead in the five-match ODI series. Gurnoor Brar has taken seven wickets in two matches, Arshdeep Singh has picked up four, and Auqib Nabi claimed two wickets in the last ODI, his first wickets in international cricket. Nabi also took six wickets for India A in the opening unofficial Test against New Zealand A, underlining why the team management wants his red-ball rhythm available in the nets. With New Zealand's own pace options already thinned on this tour, India are determined not to waste the seam and swing on offer.

The stay-back plan is part of a wider early move to Wellington. Kotak and fast-bowling coach Morne Morkel will leave for Wellington on November 11 with captain Shubman Gill, KL Rahul, Mohammed Siraj, Anshul Kamboj and Kuldeep Yadav, all of whom are in the Test squad and will not play the fourth and fifth ODIs in Mount Maunganui. The red-ball camp will run five to six practice sessions before the first Test. Arshdeep, Gurnoor and Nabi will follow a different route, staying with the ODI group through the final match and travelling to Wellington on November 16, the day after the fifth ODI, to link up with the Test contingent.

Kotak said the ODI pitches themselves have already served as preparation. "Nobody will bring Test-match adjustments into white-ball cricket," he said. "But at the same time, the pitches across both ODIs offered swing, and even after the swing subsided in four to six overs, there was seam movement, along with some awkward bounce." He added that three India A matches on the tour had helped players adapt to seam movement, grass-heavy pitches and ball behaviour, and described the overall preparation as very solid.

For the Test batters, Kotak plans scenario-based work in Wellington, simulating batting first or second and the different demands of the third and fourth innings, with individual plans for batters such as Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul, Gill and Rishabh Pant. He also stressed that the toss will be very important in these conditions.

What is next is a split week. The third ODI is played in Hamilton on Tuesday, November 10, with the fourth and fifth ODIs in Mount Maunganui on November 13 and 15. The first Test follows at the Basin Reserve in Wellington from November 19 to 23, and the second Test at Hagley Oval in Christchurch from November 27 to December 1.
